articles.title: Multi Matte Silk
articles.summary: Dead-flat matte with a faint silk fabric ripple, ultra smooth and zero gloss, in whatever colour you give it. Reads as a smooth, quiet fabric-like surface with a slight watered-silk shimmer; the ripples blur into soft cloudy light and dark patches.
articles.what: Dead-flat matte with silk micro-texture — ultra-smooth fabric feel on zero-gloss base Up close: On a neutral grey input the render is pale grey with low-contrast wavy ripples, like moire water-silk: closed loops and parallel wobbly lines 5-15 px apart over soft cloud patches 50-100 px wide. No hard edges. The red swatch is a placeholder, the finish takes the colour you give it. From a distance: Reads as a smooth, quiet fabric-like surface with a slight watered-silk shimmer; the ripples blur into soft cloudy light and dark patches. Measured spec (average): metal 13, roughness 42, coat 76. Shine: gloss. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: show car, gt / sports car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Multi Matte Silk" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: even soft texture suits every panel
Roof and hood: broad flats show the silk ripple best
Calm field, numbers in any contrasting colour read cleanly.
Stripes, graphics or fades: the low-contrast ripple lets them sit cleanly
Pairs well with: chrome trim, gold, black, white.
pitfalls: Not dead-flat matte: the old card says zero gloss, but roughness is low (42), so it shows a real highlight
Not carbon or woven cloth: ripples are wavy loops, no thread grid
Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 13 (non-metal paint), roughness 42 (high gloss), clearcoat 76 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: big dark areas in the sim, next to loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes, graphics or fades: the low-contrast ripple lets them sit cleanly; large simple shapes in contrasting colour: read well on the calm silk
Patterns to avoid: other line, weave or moire patterns: wave on wave; camo or noise: clutter with the ripples
Spec overlays that work: matte spec pattern: pushes toward the dead-flat matte the name suggests; fine sparkle flake: adds glints this finish lacks
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.what: Soft pearl zones that flash to full mirror-metallic in reactive activation regions Up close: Pastel lilac-pink and periwinkle-blue patches, 60-100 px, laid in diagonal bands under a fine wavy white net of thin crossing lines, like gauze, a woven lattice or a hairnet. Tiny white glints sit on the net. From a distance: Reads as a pale pearly lilac-blue with a delicate pink shimmer; the net fades to a silky sheen. Measured spec (average): metal 223, roughness 54, coat 186. Shine: gloss. Metal: full. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Reactive Pearl Flash" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: the net reads across broad panels
Needs a dark accent: add stripes or lower trim to anchor it
Dark navy, black or deep purple numbers read; white, pink or pale numbers vanish.
Bold dark stripes or blocks in navy, black or deep purple: contrast on the pale base
Pairs well with: black trim, dark blue, chrome.
pitfalls: Not plain white pearl: the render has distinct lilac and blue patches with a net
Not mirror chrome: it is pale and milky, with only tiny glints
Avoid: washes out in bright sim lighting, needs dark accents to read.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 223 (true metallic), roughness 54 (high gloss), clearcoat 186 (dull or trace clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: washes out in bright sim lighting, needs dark accents to read.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: bold dark stripes or blocks in navy, black or deep purple: contrast on the pale base; big graphics: simple shapes read against the fine net
Patterns to avoid: other mesh, weave or glitter patterns: moire; pale or white graphics: vanish
Spec overlays that work: matte band for numbers: calm patch; gloss clearcoat: unifies the pearl
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.summary: Concentric yellow-gold rings with a dark orange-brown metallic eye at centre, like a rippled pond or target. Reads as a large orange-and-slate ripple target, bold and clean; the rings carry well from distance, centre eye included.

The rings are squashed to a teardrop at the centre with a wide orange pool, and a fine white crackle of hair lines covers it. From a distance: Reads as a large orange-and-slate ripple target, bold and clean; the rings carry well from distance, centre eye included. Measured spec (average): metal 250, roughness 28, coat 201. The tiny hair-like flecks run at a slight diagonal and glitter pale cyan. articles.title: Rust
articles.summary: Near-black rusty brown surface with scattered glowing orange embers, pitted and rough, semi-matte with heavy sparkle. Reads as a very dark brown-black car with a barely visible warm orange dusting and a few ember-like spots; nothing like heavy rust.
articles.what: Heavy orange-brown iron oxidation with flaking corrosion texture and rough pitted surface Up close: Almost black brown ground with a fine rusty-orange dot stipple (2-3 px, evenly sprinkled) and a handful of soft out-of-focus orange glows, 20-50 px, scattered unevenly. No flakes, cracks or pitting shapes show. From a distance: Reads as a very dark brown-black car with a barely visible warm orange dusting and a few ember-like spots; nothing like heavy rust. Measured spec (average): metal 66, roughness 122, coat 63. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Rust" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Body and bumpers: even stipple works anywhere
Pair with a rust or scuff pattern on the lower panels for the real look
Dark numbers vanish; white or cream numbers read very clearly on it.
Rust, scratch or corrosion patterns in orange-brown: they supply the real decay look the base lacks
Pairs well with: matte black, cream, chrome.
pitfalls: Not real heavy rust: the old description says heavy flaking corrosion; the render is mostly black with faint orange dots
Not a bright orange-brown finish: it is very dark
Avoid: very dark, numbers need light outline, reads as dirt at small scale.

Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: very dark, numbers need light outline, reads as dirt at small scale.

articles.title: Weathered Paint
articles.summary: Sun-bleached old paint with peeling flakes and cracked clearcoat, faded and rough, in whatever colour you give it. Your colour with patchy, uneven shine: some areas metallic and glossy, others dull, like paint that has faded and worn in patches.
articles.what: Sun-damaged old paint with peeling flakes and cracking clearcoat over faded original color Up close: The paint is a flat grey with only a faint rust-brown freckle, so it takes your colour. The work is in the shine: large vertical-stretched blotches, 30-80px, that flip between full metal and none, and between glossy and rough, in all three spec panels. Real variation is strong (metal 142 plus or. From a distance: Your colour with patchy, uneven shine: some areas metallic and glossy, others dull, like paint that has faded and worn in patches. Measured spec (average): metal 142, roughness 66, coat 59. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Weathered Paint" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, sides: sun-damaged panels first
Avoid trim and small panels: blotches are 50px
No change: numbers keep your colours, and show faded sheen patches.
Rust, peel or crackle patterns: add colour to the worn patches
Pairs well with: rust brown, matte black, cream, chrome.
pitfalls: Not visible peeling flakes or cracks: the old card says that; the picture shows only blotchy shine, no cracks
Not a colour fade: paint stays flat, only the shine changes
Avoid: gloss clearcoat, small numbers.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 142 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 66 (satin gloss), clearcoat 59 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: gloss clearcoat, small numbers.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: rust, peel or crackle patterns: add colour to the worn patches; stripes and numbers: they get a faded feel under it
Patterns to avoid: clean glossy patterns, chrome or flake: fight the weathered look; other weathering overlays: redundant
Spec overlays that work: scratch or hammered spec: adds a worn texture; fine grain spec: adds micro-detail, since this is blotchy but smooth
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Worn Chrome
articles.summary: Mirror-bright metal surface broken up by cloudy patches of dull, pitted corrosion; fine grain sparkle sits under the shine. Reads as grey metal mottled with large soft stains; the white dot grain is a faint shimmer.
articles.what: Aged pitted chrome with rust spots bleeding through — decades of neglect on mirror finish Up close: Flat grey ground with soft cloudy patches, 100-250 px wide, tinted a muted green in this render, over a fine scatter of tiny bright white dots. Patch edges are soft, no pits or rust texture visible at this size. From a distance: Reads as grey metal mottled with large soft stains; the white dot grain is a faint shimmer. Measured spec (average): metal 193, roughness 49, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: high. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Worn Chrome" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, fenders, bumpers: patchy age reads on wide panels
Trim and bumpers for a believable old chrome part
Low contrast mid-grey; black or white numbers read, the patches do not break them up much.
Stripes or graphics in matte black: the mirror-and-patch look stays behind them
Pairs well with: matte black, rust brown, dull red, bare steel.
pitfalls: Not clean mirror chrome: strongly mottled with rough patches
Not a rust colour in the render: the patch tint shows green on this grey input, the rust red is claimed, not visible
Avoid: small numbers over the mottled patches, next to other high-gloss finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 193 (true metallic), roughness 49 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Metal takes on the paint colour: light and mid colours keep the sparkle, very dark colours swallow it. Avoid: small numbers over the mottled patches, next to other high-gloss finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: stripes or graphics in matte black: the mirror-and-patch look stays behind them; simple panel blocks
Patterns to avoid: other grunge, rust or weathering patterns: duplicate; fine carbon or weave: lost in the mottling
Spec overlays that work: matte or satin zones for contrast; skip sparkle spec
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
